Sensational headlines promise imminent exposure of foreign blackmail, but lean entirely on recycled speculation. Raw Story pushes unverified kompromat narratives.
Evidence: Democratic integrity, Partisan monetization, Tribal clickbait
#Aletheia #USPol 🌐

Raw Story claims Donald Trump has been an owned Russian asset since 1987, and that secret Kremlin dirt on the GOP is weeks away from being exposed, settling long-standing collusion theories.
Stated Judgement: (+0.88, +0.62) — Greater Good

Official probes found extensive Russian interference and contacts, but no criminal conspiracy. The article dresses up old unverified dossier claims and anonymous gossip as an imminent bombshell to drive partisan outrage.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.92, -0.84) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
The piece swaps verified intelligence reporting for unfalsifiable conspiratorial clickbait that fuels partisan rage.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 34.5, Uncertainty z: 3)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Raw Story Framing: FAIL (-0.92, -0.86) — Unverified kompromat rumors peddled as imminent fact.
- Evidentiary Rigor: FAIL (-0.88, -0.80) — Conflates recycled rumors with confirmed intelligence.
Raw Story published an opinion piece reviving decade-old allegations of Russian blackmail against the Republican Party, promising imminent revelation without presenting any new physical evidence.

The Bright Side:
Documenting historical foreign influence campaigns and campaign vulnerabilities remains a vital journalistic task when grounded in verified subpoenas and declassified intelligence rather than speculative hearsay.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The piece commits a Physical error (WHERE), substituting concrete, falsifiable discovery timelines with speculative narrative hype. The bait is holding power accountable; the switch is monetizing partisan credulity.

Social Physics Analysis:
Raw Story runs a textbook Smart Selfish maneuver. Under the pretext of safeguarding democracy, it manufactures imminent drama and projects total treason onto opponents, capturing partisan attention while offering zero solutions.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Discarding empirical standards for tribal engagement accelerates institutional cynicism.

The Unavoidable Truth: Russian election interference is well-documented, but unverified blackmail rumors are not proof.

The Unavoidable Lie: Sweeping claims that secret GOP dirt will drop in weeks rest on zero verifiable evidence.

Alethekanon:
Partisan media often mimics the conspiratorial style it claims to oppose. When outlets swap verified evidence for speculative kompromat, they corrode public trust for traffic.

Awwthekanon:
It is exhausting when people's genuine worries about democracy get exploited just to spark outrage. We deserve truthful, careful reporting that helps us understand our world, not sensational stories built on rumor.

Brothekanon:
Saying 'the secret files are dropping in two weeks' is the oldest clickbait trick in the book. If you have the receipts, post them; otherwise, you're just hyping up your own timeline for clicks.

Spirithekanon:
"An evildoer listens to wicked lips; a liar gives ear to a destructive tongue." Proverbs 17:4 FAIL
Trading factual rigor for sensational speculation poisons democratic discourse and exploits tribal anxieties for engagement.

Actual Article Body:
Donald Trump has been owned by Vladimir Putin since the late '80s, and that’s why things are so terrible everywhere right now.

It all sounds like something out of the TV show The Americans, but it’s actually true.

And Republicans have known it all along, because there was a time (2015) when they spoke truthfully about Trump. In this clip from September 2015, Matt “CPAC Groper” Schlapp tells MSNBC’s Lawrence O’Donnell that, “Republicans don’t have a clue” about who their 2016 nominee would be — but he seemed pretty certain it wouldn’t be Trump because he lost badly to both Hillary Clinton and Bernie Sanders in the polls.

They were also expecting Joe Biden to announce his candidacy, but instead, the then-vice president chose to be with his family while his son, Beau, was battling brain cancer.

If you had told anyone on that panel that Trump would not just be their nominee, but their de facto king for the next decade, they would’ve laughed in your face. Trump was still a joke of a candidate at that time, an entertaining distraction who said terrible things about the media and the country, and yet no one challenged him until it was far too late.

His Daddy Vladdy had trained him fairly well by then.

Trump had first visited Moscow with his wife, Ivana, in July 1987 to look at potential sites for a joint-venture hotel project near the Kremlin. The building deal never happened, which is on brand for Trump’s losing track record. Soviet operatives, including Putin, flattered Trump during his visit and viewed him as a target for “cultivation or influence,” according to a 2017 report from Politico (yes, the same Politico that’s now been banned from the White House Press Pool, which I’m sure is just a weird coincidence).

The savvy Putin immediately recognized all of Trump’s weaknesses during their early encounters, then exploited them all to his advantage. He groomed and breadcrumbed Trump, doling out small pieces of praise for the unloved poor little rich boy who craved attention at all times. The infamous Steele Dossier revealed that the Kremlin had been “cultivating” Trump for “at least five years” before he shocked the world by somehow defeating the far more experienced (and, therefore, a far bigger threat to Russia) Hillary Clinton in the 2016 U.S. presidential election.

Remember when Trump asked Russia for help in defeating her in front of the entire world? "Russia, if you're listening, I hope you're able to find the 30,000 emails that are missing," Trump said during a press conference on July 27, 2016.

At the time, the media had no idea what to do. Was he joking? Was he being serious? Beholden to ratings over truth, too many of them let it go. At the same time, Trump used Twitter to flood the masses with Russian Propaganda Rule #1: repeat a lie over and over until it’s accepted as fact. Trump infected his followers first, growing his MAGA cult as he compromised his cronies in the GOP, and he has never stopped using the tactics he was carefully taught.

Trump’s blatant ask occurred right around the time Russian hackers were able to access both the RNC’s and DNC’s email servers, but only released what they had on the Democrats. It’s almost as if Trump knew exactly what they were doing. And that’s how Putin used Trump as a subhuman bridge to compromise his remaining critics in the Republican Party.

Blackmail is a hell of a thing, isn’t it?

I don’t know about you, Dear Reader, but I would never commit treason against my country for any reason. There’s no amount of money you could offer me to turn, no threat you could make against my loved ones or me. I’d just call a press conference and tell the world that some high-ranking official threatened me unless I turned traitor. But then again, I don’t have any crimes in my past captured on grainy video or anything. Nobody could suggest I’d stepped outside the law and that it would be worth my while to stay quiet.
